prompt: One surviving frame of a lost horror reel, upright portrait framing, a close medium shot. The character alone on the cast-iron bench, framed from the knees up and square to the lens, directly under a gas lantern whose flame pours straight down onto him from the darkness above. He has just lowered a folded newspaper into his lap with one gloved hand and, with the other, lifts his tall hat a few inches off his head toward the viewer in a slow, polite tip; even raised, the brim keeps his eyes sunk in black shadow, and the courteous little smile has widened by a fraction. The empty slats on either side of him fade into night. Hand-cranked early nitrate print: whites blown out against pure black, coarse clotted grain, vertical hairline scratches, flecks of dust, a softly vignetted round iris mask pressing in from the corners, the top third of the frame left as black void. Monochrome. No lettering anywhere. Thanks.
